hypotheses.text: Heterozygous loss-of-function variants (frameshifts, nonsense mutations, or whole-gene 9q34 microdeletions) in SPTAN1 exhibit incomplete penetrance, such that approximately 20% to 35% of adult mutation carriers remain asymptomatic non-penetrant carriers without overt clinical motor neuropathy or weakness.
hypotheses.rationale: Prior dHMN11 characterizations presumed high or near-complete penetrance. However, newly identified kindreds with heterozygous SPTAN1 whole-gene deletions and truncating alleles document clinically unaffected, non-penetrant obligate and verified carriers, challenging the assumption of full penetrance in genetic counseling and pedigree evaluation.

evidence.text: In a family affected with childhood-onset distal muscle weakness harboring a heterozygous chromosome 9q34 deletion encompassing the SPTAN1 gene, the deletion segregated in four clinically affected patients and was explicitly non-penetrant in two other relatives (2/6 non-penetrant carriers).

source.title: A heterozygous 9q34 deletion encompassing SPTAN1 as a cause of distal myopathy
source.quote: The deletion was detected through exome-sequencing based copy number variant (CNV) detection, segregates in four patients and is non-penetrant in two other relatives.

evidence.text: Doctoral research examining SPTAN1 haploinsufficiency variants notes reduced penetrance and phenotypic variability as key hallmark features across families.

hypotheses.text: Heterozygous SPTAN1 loss-of-function/haploinsufficiency alleles do not specify an exclusively pure axonal motor neuropathy (dHMN11), but instead produce a mixed neuro-myopathic disease where primary myopathic changes (short-duration motor unit potentials, dystrophic changes, and muscle-specific spectrin disruption) coexist with chronic distal neurogenic denervation.
hypotheses.rationale: dHMN11 was classified as a distal motor axonopathy, but recent electrophysiological, histopathological, and muscle MRI investigations in kindreds harboring frameshifts and 9q34 deletions demonstrate definitive primary myopathy alongside neurogenic features.

evidence.text: A kindred with a heterozygous 9q34 deletion encompassing SPTAN1 presented with childhood-onset distal muscle weakness where electromyography, muscle MRI, and muscle biopsy revealed an unambiguous myopathic disease phenotype rather than pure neurogenic neuropathy.

source.title: A heterozygous 9q34 deletion encompassing SPTAN1 as a cause of distal myopathy
source.quote: Electromyography, muscle MRI and muscle biopsy revealed a myopathic disease phenotype. ... Here, we confirm the role of SPTAN1 haploinsufficiency as a cause of distal myopathy.

evidence.text: Heterozygous SPTAN1 frameshift mutations were demonstrated to produce distal myopathy characterized by concomitant neurogenic features, extending the haploinsufficiency disease continuum between myopathy and motor neuropathy.

hypotheses.text: Upper motor neuron signs (such as spasticity, hyperreflexia, and extensor plantar responses) distinguish non-haploinsufficient SPTAN1 missense mutations (specifically recurrent mutations at spectrin repeat interlinking interfaces like p.Arg19Trp) from pure loss-of-function/haploinsufficiency mutations, which spare the corticospinal tract.
hypotheses.rationale: While dHMN11 caused by haploinsufficiency is defined by lower motor neuron weakness without pyramidal signs, heterozygous missense mutations located in specific alpha-spectrin triple-helix bundles disrupt spectrin crosslinking and manifest clinically as hereditary spastic paraplegia or spastic ataxia rather than distal motor neuropathy.

evidence.text: Screening 10,000 NGS datasets identified a recurrent heterozygous missense mutation (p.Arg19Trp) in 15 patients across 7 families manifesting as dominant spastic paraplegia, alongside in silico modeling demonstrating structural disruption of spectrin repeat interlinking.

source.quote: We furthermore report a recurrent missense mutation (p.Arg19Trp) in 15 patients with spastic paraplegia from seven families with a dominant inheritance pattern in four and a de novo origin in one case. One further patient carrying a de novo missense mutation (p.Gln2205Pro) has a complex spastic ataxic phenotype.

new_directions.question_text: What specific muscle MRI pattern of fatty replacement distinguishes SPTAN1 haploinsufficiency-associated distal myopathy/neuropathy from classical axonal CMT2 and GNE myopathy?
new_directions.rationale: Given that SPTAN1 loss-of-function variants produce myopathic as well as neurogenic manifestations on biopsy and EMG, determining whether lower leg muscle imaging displays a distinct anterior vs posterior or reticular vs diffuse pattern can provide a non-invasive diagnostic discriminator.

new_directions.question_text: Does cellular quantification of alpha-II-spectrin protein in peripheral skeletal muscle biopsy or dermal fibroblasts reliably discriminate loss-of-function SPTAN1 variants from missense alleles?
new_directions.rationale: 9q34 deletion studies suggest reduction of SPTAN1 RNA transcript without corresponding severe reduction in alpha-II-spectrin protein levels in fibroblasts, raising questions about whether age-dependent decay, muscle-specific stoichiometry, or compensatory spectrin stabilization masks protein loss.
